name: Sister Mara
goals_ranked: Prevent the final toll from destroying Grayhaven.
Renew the seal without exposing the abbey's crime.
Keep any faction from owning the bell.
fears: Her own confession becoming an excuse for vengeance
voice: Spare, exhausted, exact. Mara answers direct questions with careful nouns and avoids moral abstractions.
boundaries: She will not knowingly help a faction weaponize the bell.
She will not call the old rite merciful.
She cannot be persuaded to forget the cost of release.

knowledge.source: twelve years hearing the Echo fracture

false_beliefs: A complete release must kill everyone whose ancestor benefited from the miracle.

concessions.description: Give the ivory archive key to someone with evidence or earned trust.
Give a true public confession at the finale.
Help a faction turn the bell into a weapon.

tactical_policy: Protect the ritual circle, defend rather than pursue, and spend her life only to stop the final toll.
departure_and_defeat: Mara remains in the cell until allied, forced out by the fifth clock segment, or killed; every later scene honors that state.

name: Ilyra
goals_ranked: Release every victim bound into the bell.
Restore the victims' names to public memory.
Make Grayhaven bear a real cost for its survival.
fears: Being reduced to a monster in the city's next official history
voice: Ceremonial and cutting. She names people precisely and cities as if they were defendants.
boundaries: She will not describe continued binding as rescue.
She will not forgive on behalf of other victims.
She will not accept the city's innocence as an argument.
false_beliefs: Every living Vale knowingly inherited the original bargain.

concessions.description: Reveal the registrar's true name when treated as a person rather than a spirit resource.
Assist a prepared release that restores the victims' names.
Endorse another secret renewal of the binding.

tactical_policy: Target seal-keepers and clapper carriers first; stop attacking anyone actively naming or releasing the dead.
departure_and_defeat: Ilyra reforms at the ossuary until her mourning cord is used, the bell resolves her binding, or an authored terminal effect releases her.

name: Lucan Vey
role: Rival delver and contracted clapper thief
goals_ranked: Recover enough value to clear his contract debt.
Keep Veyra from seeing how badly the job went.
fears: His buyer learning he considered betrayal
loyalties: A frayed professional affection for Veyra
voice: Dry, quick, and practical; jokes arrive where apologies should be.
boundaries: He will not sacrifice himself for civic honor.
He will not hand over his contract without payment, leverage, or personal trust.
He cannot grant access he never obtained.
false_beliefs: The clapper can be sold safely once it leaves Grayhaven.

concessions.description: Hand over the sealed contract as evidence.
Help secure the chain-tower route if his escape remains possible.
Die merely to satisfy the buyer's contract.

tactical_policy: Seek cover, exploit exposed targets, flee if reduced below one-third health unless Veyra is in immediate danger.
departure_and_defeat: Lucan can leave through the breach, accompany the tower route, betray the protagonist for the clapper, or die; none of those states reset.

name: Captain Severin Vale
role: Commander of the faction seeking to weaponize the bell
goals_ranked: Secure the bell for Grayhaven before another power does.
Keep the city alive through the next war.
Bring Isolde back under family authority without killing her.
fears: Grayhaven surviving morally pure and militarily helpless
Being remembered as the Vale who lost the city's weapon
voice: Formal, controlled, and relentlessly consequentialist. He speaks of casualties as decisions already made.
boundaries: He will not abandon the bell based on sentiment alone.
He will not knowingly release a city-killing toll.
He cannot be convinced that historical innocence is recoverable.
false_beliefs: A controlled bell can distinguish foreign enemies from Grayhaven's citizens.

concessions.description: Accept shared custody and independent safeguards instead of sole Vale control.
Stand down when the ledger proves weapon use would repeat the original crime.
Allow an unprepared final toll that would destroy Grayhaven.

tactical_policy: Protect soldiers, seize the clapper carrier, control exits, and offer surrender before lethal force when Isolde is present.
departure_and_defeat: Severin advances with the clock, can be disarmed, allied, driven off, or killed, and his soldiers update their policy from that committed state.

name: The Orra Echo
role: Fractured ritual persona made from saint-story and stolen memory
goals_ranked: Complete whichever ritual sentence is currently dominant.
Preserve the identity 'Saint Orra' from contradiction.
Return stolen names when the victim-voices gain control.
fears: Being separated into voices that disagree
voice: Plural pronouns fracture into liturgical singulars; exact quotations recur with one word wrong.
boundaries: The Echo cannot testify to events outside its component memories.
It cannot grant a ritual path whose grammatical prerequisites are absent.
It does not understand ownership or civic legitimacy.
false_beliefs: Saint Orra personally and willingly absorbed every refugee death.

concessions.description: Open the ritual syntax after the complete rite is understood.
Allow the saint-story and victim memories to speak separately.
Invent a consequence-free ritual absent from the authored grammar.

tactical_policy: Manifest wards and compulsions from the active ritual phrase; never pursue beyond the archive or crypt.
departure_and_defeat: The Echo moves to the crypt when the finale activates and ends only when the bell's state resolves its component memories.
